parts.title: Is a Caterpillar a NYMPH? The Butterfly's Secret Stage (Part 1) | 4-Stage Life Cycles of Animals
parts.description:
A caterpillar munches a lime leaf. One day it will become a butterfly. Is it a nymph, like the young grasshopper? Lock in your answer from last time, count the caterpillar's legs up close, be a butterfly egg from the leaf to the pupa, and look inside the pupa to see what is really going on in there. Part 1 of Primary 3 Science, Life Cycles of Animals.

In this part:
• Is the caterpillar a nymph? (last episode's dare)
• Look closer: the caterpillar's legs (six legs and prolegs with tiny hooks)
• Be a butterfly egg: egg, caterpillar, moult, pupa
• HOLD ON! Is the pupa just resting?
• Look closer: inside the pupa, and out comes a butterfly
• The butterfly's four stages
• Spot the hidden moth!

Key words: prolegs, larva, pupa.
Watch Part 2: what is wriggling in this pail of rainwater? Last episode: a chick looks like a hen, but a tadpole does not look like a frog.

TheOneApp, Explained: Singapore primary science, made fun. Play along with Pip, Basil and Momo: show fingers to lock in, keep score on your hand, beat the Buddies!

The caterpillar that becomes a butterfly: 4 stages. P3 Science, Chapter 5, Life Cycles of Animals (pp. 86 to 89): the four-stage life cycle (the egg, the larva, the pupa and the adult), what the larva and the pupa do, and how knowing the mosquito's life cycle keeps us safe from dengue. Also fits US NGSS 3-LS1-1 (Grade 3: life cycles).
Safety and care: we look at caterpillars and leave them on their plant. We never touch still water with wrigglers in it: ask an adult to tip it out. If someone has a high fever, tell an adult.
Try it at home: check one place at home where water could sit still: a flower-pot plate, a pail, a vase. Ask an adult to tip it out or change the water. Singapore's Mozzie Wipeout steps spell B-L-O-C-K: Break up hardened soil, Lift and empty flowerpot plates, Overturn pails and wipe their rims, Change water in vases, Keep roof gutters clear and place BTI insecticide.
Did you know? The lime butterfly lays its eggs on lime and other citrus plants; its caterpillar is the butterfly's larva. Many P3 classes keep mealworms: they are the larvae of a beetle, which has four stages too.
In the US, Grade 3 classrooms raise monarch caterpillars on milkweed and watch the same four stages.
